entries.title: Asian stock markets climb after earlier tech rout
entries.summary: Markets rebound after tech rout triggered by Democrats' sweeping victory in US midterm elections.
entries.content:
Markets rebound after tech rout triggered by Democrats’ sweeping victory in US midterm elections.

Asian stock markets have rebounded after last week’s tech rout triggered by the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.

Key indexes in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong made substantial gains on Monday, following a rebound on Wall Street on Friday.

In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei 225 was up 3.45 percent as of 04:00 GMT.

In Taipei, the Taiex was 5.72 percent higher, while the Kospi in Seoul was up 1.68 percent.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index was up 0.19 percent.

Futures for Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 index and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 were up 0.60 percent and 0.59 percent, respectively.

They had dipped earlier following US-based chip giant Nvidia’s announcement that it would investigate its CEO over a romantic relationship he conducted with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia’s board of directors said that while it had confidence in CEO Jensen Huang and had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised, an independent inquiry would examine “all available information”.

The board said Huang supported the inquiry and pledged his full cooperation.

“The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said.

The stock market rebound comes after the US midterm results prompted a $2.5 trillion sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday amid concerns that Democratic-controlled legislatures could slow the rollout of data centres used to power AI.

The tech rout spilled into Asia on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 and Kospi plunging about 6 percent and 9 percent, respectively, and the Hang Seng Index dropping more than 1 percent.

entries.title: Rubio says war on Iran unpopular but ‘necessary’ to stop nuclear threat
entries.summary: US secretary of state says Iran's negotiation demands are 'outrageous and ridiculous, and really not realistic'.
entries.content:
US secretary of state says Iran’s negotiation demands are ‘outrageous and ridiculous, and really not realistic’.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran to safeguard the world from Tehran’s nuclear ambitions.

Rubio told reporters in Florida on Sunday that Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and had worked to stop it from pursuing a nuclear weapon.

Trump addressed “difficult challenges for the security of our country – doing it isn’t necessarily popular, but necessary”, Rubio added.

On diplomatic efforts to end the war, Rubio said, “I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough”. He added that although Trump prefers a diplomatic solution, Iranian demands are “not just unacceptable, but in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”.

Rubio comments came after Trump had said that “a lot of people didn’t like” Vice President JD Vance recent comments blaming the US-led war on Iran for the Republican Party’s crushing defeat in last week’s US midterm elections.

Trump said that although he mostly agreed with Vance, he did not regret the decision to go to war against Iran. It “will go down as one of the best things we ever did”, he said, adding that if Tehran were to have a nuclear weapon, “they would blow up the world”.

Trump also told CNN in a phone interview on Sunday that as long as Washington sees progress in negotiations with Tehran and they sign a “strong agreement”, it is “highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary” for the US to resume strikes.

For Iran’s part, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that it was “time for the White House to make its own” decision on the war.

“American voters have made their choice,” Araghchi wrote on X, referring to the midterm election results.

He added that Tehran’s “2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results”.

“Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell.”

Iran has offered to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping within two days if the United States meets its conditions.

Trump is set to meet Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani at the White House on Monday, according to his official schedule.

Tehran is reviewing proposals presented by Qatar aimed at addressing differences with Washington, according to the Associated Press news agency.

In recent days, Rubio has also denied “unfounded” speculation that he was quitting as the top US diplomat to run for higher office in 2028.

entries.title: Mexico arrests alleged major leader of Jalisco cartel
entries.summary: Rafael Alvarez, alias 'R2', was captured with intelligence shared by the ⁠US Drug Enforcement Administration.
entries.content:
Rafael Alvarez, alias ‘R2’, was captured with intelligence shared by the ⁠US Drug Enforcement Administration.

Authorities in Mexico have announced the arrest of an alleged leader in the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), one of the country’s two main criminal groups.

Rafael Alvarez, alias “R2”, who is suspected of heading CJNG’s “Los Rs” cell, was arrested in an operation in the city of Zapopan, in the Guadalajara metropolitan area, on Sunday, as a result of intelligence shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)⁠, according to Mexico’s Navy.

“This cell is mainly ⁠linked to extortion, drug trafficking, homicide, illegal deprivation of liberty, kidnapping and attacks against authorities,” Mexico’s Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said.

He added that victims of the group’s extortion included “business owners and avocado producers”.

Harfuch said on X that Alvarez was wounded in a shootout that broke out during the arrest and is receiving medical care.

Alvarez has an outstanding arrest warrant in Mexico for aggravated homicide and another warrant for ⁠extradition to the US, Harfuch also said.

Authorities, including those from Mexico’s National Intelligence Center, also took part in the operation, which captured 19 other people.

Alvarez is linked to the killing of at least 19 people, including last year’s murder of Carlos Manzo, the popular crime-fighting mayor of Uruapan in Mexico’s avocado-producing Michoacan state.

The CJNG, which operates in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan, was designated a “foreign terrorist organisation” by the US government in 2025 and is known for violent tactics and attacks on authorities.

It competes with the Sinaloa Cartel for drug trafficking into the US.

Since the death of the CJNG founder, Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, in a military operation in February, several of its top leaders have been apprehended.

But there are still reports of kidnapping for ransom in the areas where the cartels are active.

An estimated 134,000 people are believed to be missing across Mexico, with Jalisco recording the country’s highest numbers of disappearances.

entries.title: Moldova launches new power line to Romania to cut reliance on Russia
entries.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu says 'two more power lines to Romania are on the way'.
entries.content:
Moldovan President Maia Sandu says ‘two more power lines to Romania are on the way’.

Moldova has officially launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid to reduce its reliance on Russian energy.

“For decades, Moscow used energy to blackmail us,” Moldovan President Maia Sandu said on X on Sunday.

“No more: Moldova buys zero Russian gas,” she added.

Moldova, a country of 2.6 million people wedged between Romania and Ukraine, received most of its gas from Russia via its pro-Moscow separatist region of Transnistria and pipelines running through Ukraine.

“Thanks to this project, we are strengthening our electricity transmission capacity, diversifying our means of supply and reinforcing the connection of the Republic of Moldova to the European energy system,” Sandu said during the power line’s inauguration ceremony on Sunday in the capital, Chisinau.

She also said that “two more power lines to Romania are on the way”.

European Commissioner for Energy Marta Kos, who was at the ceremony, said Moldova could now “buy energy where it is cheapest”.

The 400-kilowatt extra-high-voltage line, which runs from the city of Vulcanesti to Chisinau, allows Moldova to cut reliance on the Cuciurgan thermal power plant in Transnistria.

“Every time Moldova dares to choose something other than what Moscow wants, they threaten to cut our electricity,” said Sandu.

Dubbed the “energy independence line”, the power grid was launched two years after the date Moldovan authorities initially promised.

Last month, Moldova’s parliament approved a government-requested state of emergency until November 20 as it tries to ease gas shortages amid soaring world energy prices.

Some in Europe have blamed Moscow for the skyrocketing gas prices, accusing it of withholding additional supplies to put pressure on the continent.

European-aligned states in the Black Sea region say they are experiencing renewed attacks allegedly carried out by Russia.

Last month, Romania blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast, killing one crew member and leaving three others missing.

Ukraine, Romania and Bulgaria have called on NATO to “fast-track the additional surveillance capabilities” to protect commercial shipping in the Black Sea, as fighting in Russia’s war on Ukraine escalates.

NATO said it would send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems and drones to the ⁠⁠⁠⁠Black Sea.

entries.title: Drone attack suspends production at Iraq’s Khor Mor gasfield
entries.summary: The strike leaves more than 70 percent of northern Iraq's Kurdish region without power.
entries.content:
The strike leaves more than 70 percent of northern Iraq’s Kurdish region without power.

A drone attack on the Khor Mor gasfield in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region of northern Iraq has caused a fire at the facility and cut power to the region, according to Iraqi and Kurdish officials.

The Sunday night attack left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power.

It was not clear who was responsible for the attack or whether it was related to the United States and Israel’s war on Iran.

Al Jazeera’s fact-checking agency Sanad has verified footage of smoke and flames rising from the vicinity of the gasfield in the Sulaimaniyah governorate.

Omid Ahmed, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government’s Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in the cities of Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal and Duhok, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The strike knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of electricity generation off the grid, he said.

He added that the ministry would provide electricity to critical facilities, such as hospitals and water treatment plants, by operating hydroelectric power stations and other plants that run on alternative fuel.

Al Jazeera’s Peter Smith, reporting from Baghdad, cited security sources as saying the explosive-laden drone struck the Khor Mor gas storage facility, reducing the energy grid’s capacity by 70 to 80 percent.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said there were no casualties as a result of the attack, based on an initial assessment, the INA reported.

Al-Zaidi also directed that a joint investigative committee be formed with the relevant authorities in the Kurdish region to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, INA reported.

The attack comes amid heightened regional tensions. A drone strike hit the same facility last year, with no group having claimed responsibility.

entries.title: Jeffries backs Hegseth impeachment as Democrats vow probes of Trump allies
entries.summary: Democratic lawmakers are mapping out their post-midterm agenda with pledges to lead committee investigations into Trump.
entries.content:
Democratic lawmakers are mapping out their post-midterm agenda with pledges to lead committee investigations into Trump and his officials.

United States House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has thrown his support behind impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, as the Democratic Party prepares to use its incoming congressional majorities to probe President Donald Trump’s administration.

In a Sunday appearance on the Television show This Week with George Stephanopoulos, Jeffries weighed in on the upcoming impeachment resolution, anticipated for the coming days.

“I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said. “The so-called secretary of defence has abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.”

The impeachment resolution has been spearheaded by outgoing Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, a vocal critic of the US-Israel war on Iran.

“Pete Hegseth has got to go,” Jeffries added. “I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution.”

Investigating ‘unprecedented corruption’

Jeffries is poised to become the next speaker in the House of Representatives after Democrats notched a historic victory in the November 3 midterm elections.

Both the House and the Senate flipped into Democratic control, with the left-wing party making some of its biggest gains in the lower chamber in more than half a century.

Democrats are expected to use their new congressional majorities to launch investigations into the Trump administration.

There have also been concerns, voiced by Trump himself, that he and other top officials could face impeachment.

In Sunday’s interview, Jeffries said the Democratic majority would move “aggressively” in its first 100 days in office, both to address affordability and “unprecedented corruption” under Trump.

“We are committed to cleaning up the mess wherever it’s found,” Jeffries said. “That’s in Congress, in the Supreme Court, and with respect to this administration.”

Currently, Republicans hold a government “trifecta”, with control of both chambers of Congress and the presidency. The Supreme Court also boasts a conservative supermajority, shaped by three Trump appointees.

But a new Congress will be sworn in on January 3. In the coming weeks, Democrats will choose their party leaders for both chambers.

Representative Robert Garcia formally announced his bid to lead the House Oversight Committee in a letter to colleagues on Thursday.

The committee is the chamber’s principal investigative panel, with the power to subpoena witnesses and documents.

‘Very serious’ allegations

On Sunday, Garcia told CNN that Stephen Miller‘s influential role in the Trump administration warranted investigation.

Miller, who was named last week as White House chief of staff, has been closely associated with Trump’s hardline immigration policies since his first term as president.

“What we think is that Stephen Miller is the architect of this horrific, unjust policy happening across the country,” Garcia said, pointing to policies of separating immigrant families and accusations of due process abuses.

“Stephen Miller is at the centre of major policy decisions that are happening in the administration, and it does deserve oversight and investigation.”

Garcia also signalled interest in questioning businessman Elon Musk over his leadership in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), a federal initiative that led to widespread federal workforce cuts at the start of Trump’s second term.

DOGE also sought access to sensitive government data, including Americans’ personal information.

“What happened with DOGE, in particular, and the federal employees losing jobs the way they did and people’s data likely being compromised, I think, is very serious,” Garcia said.

Congressional committees have the power to hold hearings, subpoena witnesses, and demand documents, giving lawmakers a constitutional check on the executive branch.

The House can also impeach administration officials if a simple majority votes in favour.

Conviction and removal, however, require a two-thirds vote in the Senate, a high bar even with Democrats controlling the chamber.

Trump’s camp bites back

The White House was quick to draw its own battle lines.

Speaking on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said there could be investigations into Democratic lawmakers over their “threatening” rhetoric.

He added he was ready to counter Democratic efforts to probe and impeach Trump officials.

“If that’s what this new incoming leadership wants to do, we are ready,” said Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Trump. “If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer. It’s me.”

Trump, meanwhile, made similar remarks in a Truth Social post on Saturday.

He called on the Justice Department to investigate Democrats over their plans to haul his allies before congressional committees, branding them as “SLEAZEBAGS” who “should go to jail”.

“The threats being made by the Democrat Party against innocent Republican Donors and Party Members are absolutely unprecedented, and totally illegal,” the president wrote.
